title: Add xtask repin command and point the version refusal at it
summary: The pin stays exact. I added one command, `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`, that reads the installed claude's version and rewrites `claude_version` in athena.toml. The driver's refusal in `check_pinned` now tells the operator to run it. The audience is the operator who repins by hand after each Claude Code update.

defaults_applied.how: Command and tests are Rust in xtask and athena-agent.
Unit tests for the version rewrite and the refusal text; cargo test and clippy pass.
Tests run the rewrite on sample TOML text and assert the resulting file content and refusal message.
One command plus one message change, with no change to the exact-match rule.
Usage text, README note and CHANGELOG entry are written for an outside operator.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check, and cargo run -p xtask for the usage text.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The command is an xtask subcommand named `repin`, next to `setup`, `ci` and `site`, so it needs no running Athena job.
It runs `claude --version` on the claude found on PATH, and falls back to the private install if there is none.
It edits only the `claude_version` line in athena.toml and keeps the rest of the file, including comments. The edit is a line-level replace, not a re-serialization.
The command does not commit. The operator reviews and commits the one-line change.
The athena.toml pin value is not changed by this work; only the command changes it, when the operator runs it.
The refusal message in check_pinned changes from 'run ./setup.sh' to name the repin command. When the installed version differs, the message says to repin to it.
The command is idempotent: if the installed version already equals the pin, it reports that and changes nothing. It refuses an unparseable version or a missing claude.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test on the athena.toml rewrite function shows that given text with `claude_version = "2.1.299"` and a new version `2.1.301`, only that line changes and every other line, including comments, is byte-identical. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
Tests show the repin logic refuses empty or unparseable version output, and makes no change when the installed version already equals the pin. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.

A test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs shows `check_pinned` still returns an error for a stand-in binary reporting a version other than the pin, and that the error names both versions and the exact repin command `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`. A matching version is still accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.
`cargo run -p xtask -- foo` (an unknown subcommand) prints a usage text that lists `repin`.  `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
README.md or docs describe the post-update flow for an operator: after Claude Code updates, run `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`, then commit the one-line athena.toml change. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
The exact-match rule is unchanged. athena.toml, defaults.toml and .github/workflows are not edited by the change itself, and no secrets or personal data are committed.

out_of_scope: Accepting a range of Claude Code versions (patch or 2.x); the pin stays exact.
Auto-repinning at job start or from inside an Athena job.
Installing a different Claude Code version; the command only records the installed one.
